title: Rate Limiter Audit
summary: An API gateway's access log must be audited against its rate limit. Fix requests landing in the wrong window, replay the limiter to find rejections, then audit a full day of traffic in time.
followUps: Why does multiplying 2.006 by 1000 not give 2006, and which other timestamps are affected?
Why must rejected requests not count towards the window, and what would a client see if they did?
What is the cost of rejections for one client with n requests, and how much memory does it hold at once?
The gateway runs on four machines that each keep their own window. What changes, and what would you do about it?
What did the assistant get wrong or leave out, and how did you notice?
